title: The Press That Changed the World
passage:
Before the fifteenth century, most books in Europe were copied by hand. A skilled writer might spend many months producing a single copy, so books were rare and very expensive, and only a small number of people owned them.

Around 1440, a German metalworker named Johannes Gutenberg began working on a faster method in the city of Mainz. He created small metal pieces called movable type, each carrying one raised letter. Workers arranged the letters into lines and pages, covered them with ink, and pressed paper firmly against them. When a page was finished, the letters could be taken apart and reused for the next page.

Gutenberg combined several ideas to make his system work. He developed an oily ink that stuck well to metal, and he adapted the screw press that farmers used for squeezing grapes and olives. Around 1455, his workshop completed a famous Bible, printing about one hundred and eighty copies.

Gutenberg was not the first person to print with movable type. Centuries earlier, printers in China and Korea had used type made of clay and metal. However, his press spread quickly across Europe, and within fifty years printing shops operated in hundreds of cities.

As books became cheaper, more people learned to read, and new ideas in science and education travelled faster than ever before.

questions.stem: Which word belongs to the same word family as "print"?
options: printer
paper
pressed
pages
questions.why: "Printer" is built from the root word "print"; the other words have different roots.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the word "rare" correctly, with the same meaning as in the passage?
options: She rare the heavy book carefully to her brother.
Snow is rare in Riyadh, so people photograph it.
The rare of the shop opens every morning at nine.
They rare quickly across the field to the ball.
questions.why: In the passage "rare" means not common; only this sentence uses it as an adjective meaning "seldom found."

questions.stem: Why were books expensive before the printing press?
options: Paper could only be bought from merchants in China.
Kings did not allow ordinary people to own books.
Ink was made from expensive gold and silver powder.
Each copy had to be written by hand over many months.
questions.why: The first paragraph explains that a copy might take months to write by hand, so books were rare and costly.

questions.stem: Which step came LAST in printing a page with Gutenberg's method?
options: Workers arranged the letters into lines.
The letters were taken apart to be reused.
The letters were covered with ink.
Paper was pressed against the inked letters.
questions.why: The passage says that when a page was finished, the letters were taken apart and reused for the next page.

questions.stem: What effect did cheaper books have, according to the passage?
options: More people learned to read.
Fewer printing shops were opened.
Writers stopped copying by hand at once.
Farmers stopped using screw presses.
questions.why: The last paragraph links cheaper books to more people learning to read.

questions.stem: The writer says new ideas "travelled faster than ever before." What does this expression mean?
options: Ideas were carried by fast horses.
Scientists began to travel more often.
Ideas reached many people much more quickly.
Books were thrown from city to city.
questions.why: Ideas cannot really travel; the phrase means printed books spread knowledge quickly to many readers.

questions.stem: Which event could really have happened in the fifteenth century?
options: A printer sent finished pages to another city by email.
A printer reused the same metal letters for a new page.
A machine printed hundreds of books without any ink.
Gutenberg read a printed newspaper online every day.
questions.why: Reusing movable type is described in the passage; the other events depend on modern technology.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST expresses the writer's viewpoint about the printing press?
options: It was a failure that few people used.
It was invented by Gutenberg alone with no earlier ideas.
It helped knowledge spread widely in Europe.
It made books more expensive than before.
questions.why: The writer shows the press spreading to hundreds of cities and helping ideas travel, while noting earlier printers in Asia.

questions.stem: Which information in the passage is the LEAST complete?
options: Where Gutenberg built and operated his first press
What material his movable type letters were made of
How the earlier printers in China and Korea did their work
How many copies of the famous Bible were printed
questions.why: The passage only mentions the Asian printers in one sentence and gives no details of their methods.

questions.stem: Which is the BEST alternative title for the passage?
options: The Daily Life of Grape Farmers in Germany
Why Books Will Always Be Very Expensive
Learning to Write Beautifully by Hand
Letters That Moved: How Printing Changed Europe
questions.why: The passage explains movable type and its effects on Europe, which this title captures.
